name: Internal clause-by-clause workshops (11 business units)
note: The first pass over the register. Every clause gets an owning unit and a disposition.

name: Held-over items surgery with unit managers
note: Bring the parked items into the open and force a decision: in scope, out of scope, or deferred with a stated reason.

name: Community issues survey — what is and is not working
note: Issues stage, before positions are fixed. Reaching people early is what makes the statutory exhibition defensible later.

name: Trader and business roundtables
audience: Chapel St, Glenferrie Rd, High St, Toorak Village
note: Footpath trading, parklets, signage, filming and street events.

name: Deliberative panel on the contested items
note: Reserved for the genuinely contested items: cat containment, amplified music hours, alcohol-free areas.

name: Targeted sessions — Disability Advisory Committee and multicultural groups
note: Accessible footpath width, signage, and how directive powers are experienced.

name: Rough sleeping and outreach sector session
audience: Homelessness services, Victoria Police, outreach providers
note: Camping clauses and the operating protocol that sits behind them. Feeds the Charter assessment directly.

name: Youth and sport user groups
audience: Reserve user groups, clubs, young people
note: Reserve restrictions, ball games, skating, drones, personal training.

name: Close the loop — what we heard and what changed
note: Published before positions go to Councillors, not after. Participants should see their input in the options paper.

name: Statutory public notice and exhibition of the proposed local law
note: The formal step. Notice of purpose and general purport, copies available, submission period. Confirm the notice and submission requirements with Governance against the Act and the Governance Rules.

name: Hearing of submitters
audience: Submitters who ask to be heard
note: Allow for a dedicated committee meeting. Volume is the variable — cat containment could carry this on its own.

name: Commencement communications and permit-holder transition
note: Existing permits under cl.184 run a year from issue, so some will straddle commencement. Transitional arrangements must be drafted, not improvised.
